intended_object: The class of finite Kripke frames whose accessibility relation is transitive and irreflexive, i.e. the finite strict partial orders. This is the frame class that characterizes the provability logic GL (axiom L, Löb). Inferred from the name and from the `DefinedByL` instance in the same file.
explanation: In this library a `FiniteFrame` is a Kripke `Frame` whose set of worlds is `Finite`, and a `FiniteFrameClass` is a `Set FiniteFrame`. The definition picks out the frames whose relation satisfies `IsTrans` and `Std.Irrefl`, which is exactly the class of finite transitive irreflexive frames. On a finite frame, transitive plus irreflexive is the same as transitive plus conversely well-founded, which is the standard frame condition for GL. The file uses this class to prove that axiom L defines it. Mathlib has no modal Kripke frame classes, so there is no counterpart. The notion is a specific frame class built on the library's own frame setup, so it is not too narrow.
